---
id: "smk-15"
title: "Fortran"
---

Fortran is a programming language designed for numerical and scientific computing. It was developed by a team at IBM led by John Backus and first delivered in 1957, which makes it one of the oldest high-level languages still in use. The name is a contraction of 'formula translation'. Early versions introduced features such as the DO loop and the arithmetic IF statement, and the language has been revised repeatedly: Fortran 77 added structured control flow, Fortran 90 added free-form source, modules, array operations and dynamic memory, and later standards added object-oriented programming and coarrays for parallelism. Fortran compilers are known for generating fast code for array-heavy calculations, and the language remains common in weather forecasting, computational physics, chemistry and the numerical libraries on which other languages depend. Many benchmark programs used to rank supercomputers are written in Fortran.
